encounters.title: Lanterns on the Raft
encounters.flavor: The raft keeps circling the landing, every post hung with a lantern burning in daylight. The ferryman raises his largest light whenever the current runs dark beneath the middle pier. Behind you, a family with two bundles waits in the sun. Their youngest has begun to cry quietly, and none of them dares call him closer.

choices.label: Steady the mooring rope
choices.intent: Wade in and hold the raft against the current so the family can board.
choices.risk: If the line slips, the raft takes the family downstream with nobody to steady it.

success.text: You set your heels in the mud and hold. One by one the family steps across, the youngest clutching a lantern from the rail. Someone presses a packet of river cakes into your hand without a word.

failure.text: The wet rope runs through your palms and tears them open. The family climbs aboard before the raft pulls clear, its youngest looking back at the hand you cannot lift to wave. You cross alone after dark, gripping each rail with bandaged fingers.

choices.label: Ask why the lantern burns
choices.intent: Call across the water and ask the ferryman what the daylight lantern is for.
choices.risk: The ferryman can take a question as help, or as one more reason to leave them waiting.

success.text: The ferryman poles closer and speaks low: a sunken channel opens only when the current stills, and the lantern tells him when to wait. You keep the lesson, and the family boards on his next pass.

failure.text: He hears a jeer where you meant none and pushes off hard. You spend the hot afternoon trudging the bank for another crossing and end the day footsore, still on the wrong side of the river.

encounters.title: The Toll of Two Names
encounters.flavor: At the landing a registrar takes no coin, only each traveler's name. The toll book lies open between a lantern and an inkstone, and the same two names appear again and again, years apart, written in different hands. The woman ahead of you whispers hers. When the registrar writes it down, the line behind you falls silent.

choices.label: Demand an honest account
choices.intent: Put your hand on the ledger and ask her plainly what those repeated names mean.
choices.risk: The guards are close enough to hear a raised voice; the next person in line will pay for a closed gate.

success.text: The registrar turns back the pages. The names of travelers lost in the current have been copied forward as debts owed by those who survived them. She has been recording absence as a toll. She strikes your entry from the book, then puts her hand over the next blank line so the waiting family cannot see it.

failure.text: She whistles once and the guards come running. You back away before the gate can close on you, but the crowd crushes in from every side and you come out of it bruised and shaken.

choices.label: Copy the ledger quietly
choices.intent: Read over the registrar's shoulder and quietly copy the altered dates into memory.
choices.risk: One careless move, and the guards will see what you are doing.

success.text: You fix the altered dates in your head and slip through with the line. Somewhere in those numbers is the answer to one old disappearance, and now you carry it with you.

failure.text: Your sleeve catches a wax seal on the ledger and tears it loose. The guards push in while the queue scatters. An elbow catches you hard; by the time you reach open ground, the food from your pack lies trampled in the river mud. The altered dates remain in the book.

encounters.title: The Boat That Waits
encounters.flavor: An empty skiff sits tied to a post long after the other boats have gone. The boatwright says its owner promised to come back before the flood, yet the water has fallen twice since. Every plank is sound except the rudder, which is splintered and half mended, as if someone left in a hurry.

choices.label: Repair the rudder
choices.intent: Borrow the boatwright's tools and fit the waiting skiff with a sound rudder.
choices.risk: If your repair fails midstream, the waiting skiff will carry somebody toward the snags.

success.text: The skiff takes the current cleanly on its trial run. Pleased, the boatwright packs you a bundle of dried fish and tells you where the shallows run safe and steady.

failure.text: A hidden crack splits under strain, and the tiller swings back hard into your foot. You limp to the bank and watch the skiff drift away downriver, as empty as when you found it.

choices.label: Wait for its owner
choices.intent: Sit by the post with the boatwright and see who finally comes for the skiff.
choices.risk: You spend a meal and a night waiting for someone who may be dead.

success.text: Near dusk the owner's sister comes down the bank, coat hem dark with mud. She has no fare and no claim on the skiff, only the truth: her brother went after the missing river patrol and never returned. The boatwright looks toward the broken rudder and says he should have asked sooner.

failure.text: Night falls and no one comes. You eat a meal you meant to save just to keep going through the vigil, and at first light you find only a second rope, coiled and never used, beneath the seat.

encounters.title: Weighed in Salt
encounters.flavor: At the trading post, a merchant weighs out salt by the spoon on a brass scale while a queue of hungry travelers looks on. Each new customer gets a little less than the one before. The merchant blames the shifting floorboards, and nobody in line has the strength left to argue.

choices.label: Test the counterweights
choices.intent: Ask to hold the brass weights yourself and feel whether they are honest.
choices.risk: If you expose the merchant, his hired hands can turn a public scale into a private beating.

success.text: The brass weight is hollow and light. You split its seam and a pebble drops onto the counter. The merchant measures the salt again under the eyes of everyone in the queue. The woman behind you presses bread and a twist of salt into your palm; he will remember whose hand opened the weight.

failure.text: Before you can prove anything, the merchant's hired hands grab you by the collar and throw you into a stack of crates. You pick yourself up sore and empty-handed while the line shuffles forward.

choices.label: Trade supplies for passage
choices.intent: Bargain calmly for a crossing voucher instead of fighting over spoonfuls of salt.
choices.risk: He can take your food and sell you a voucher no ferryman honors.

success.text: You keep your voice even and your offer small. Eager to be rid of a patient customer, the merchant stamps a sealed crossing voucher and lets you keep your last provisions.

failure.text: The merchant smiles, weighs your goods out twice, and keeps both measures. You walk away short of food for the trail ahead and no closer to a crossing.

encounters.title: The Mended Compass
encounters.flavor: A cartographer offers to trade a compass she has mended with wire and patience for a map of the old delta. She admits she has redrawn the river six times. A neat new chart is pinned to her table, and the sixth draft, half erased, lies folded beneath her stool where she will not look at it.

choices.label: Compare the two charts
choices.intent: Unfold the old draft beside the neat chart and look for what she erased.
choices.risk: The erased bend may be the only true one, but choosing it means ignoring every newer map.

success.text: The erased riverbend lines up with a stone marker you passed that morning. The cartographer goes quiet, then hands you a full water skin and the old draft, saying it is safer in your pack than in hers.

failure.text: You follow the neat chart as far as a bridge that washed away last season. From the reeds you can still see the cartographer's old erased line, pointing to a passage you passed hours ago. By the time you reach it, the sun is gone and your strength with it.

choices.label: Help reset the compass
choices.intent: Help her settle the mended compass so its needle points true again.
choices.risk: A needle that points toward the table instead of north will lead travelers astray.

success.text: The needle shivers and steadies. She thanks you by marking three cairns on your map, ones she says she trusts more than any river she has ever drawn.

failure.text: A lodestone hidden in her table drags the needle off true, and you do not find it until the work is done wrong. You leave her a meal from your pack for the wasted afternoon and walk on with a bearing you cannot trust.

encounters.title: Three Cups on the Table
encounters.flavor: A cook sets three cups of broth on the table in front of you: one for the buyer, one for a traveler who never came back, and one for whoever asks no questions. Two armed patrons at the next bench watch to see which cup you lift. The cook's own bowl sits by the stove, untouched.

choices.label: Share the untouched meal
choices.intent: Carry the cook's untouched bowl to her and ask her to eat with you.
choices.risk: If you give the cook her untouched bowl, the armed patrons will see whom you have chosen.

success.text: You carry the cook's untouched bowl from beside the stove and sit with her while the three cups cool on the table. After a few spoonfuls she describes a back road around the false checkpoint. She wraps bread for your journey, but will not say whom she was waiting to feed.

failure.text: The patrons take the gesture as an insult and kick the table over. Hot broth and broken cups go everywhere, and you are left bruised, kneeling in the scraps.

choices.label: Question the armed patrons
choices.intent: Leave the cups where they stand and ask the patrons about the traveler who never returned.
choices.risk: They are guarding an answer, and the cook is close enough to suffer for your question.

success.text: Their story of a vanished caravan does not match the cook's. Between the two accounts you find the lie: the checkpoint downriver is false, set up to strip whoever passes through it.

failure.text: One patron spits on the floor and draws a knife. You get out the door ahead of the blade, but the long run around the post in the heat leaves you winded and the day half gone.

encounters.title: Footprints in the Silt
encounters.flavor: A surveyor crouches beside a line of footprints pressed, still wet, into the silt. They begin in a dry channel and stop at an empty bank. His row of stakes marks last season's waterline, but fresh mud lies higher than any of them, and he wants help checking the next marker before the light goes.

choices.label: Follow the wet prints
choices.intent: Follow the wet prints across the channel to learn where the walker went.
choices.risk: The trail crosses salt that looks solid until it swallows a boot.

success.text: The footprints end at a concealed spillway where the buried river surfaces. You test each stone before marking a crossing above the silt, and call the surveyor over to see it. When the channel fills again, travelers will have a different road because you stopped to look.

failure.text: The salt crust breaks beneath your feet and the silt takes you to the knees. You claw your way out, scraped and shaking, and by the time you can stand the prints are gone.

choices.label: Help set new markers
choices.intent: Hold the stakes steady while the surveyor drives them in above the new mud.
choices.risk: The channel can fill without warning while you work.

success.text: Together you set the stakes at the new line. The surveyor shares his water skin and a hard biscuit, and a warning worth more than either: the next channel floods at dusk.

failure.text: A surge tears the rope away and takes the surveyor's tools. You drag him onto the high bank before the water reaches the last stake. Both of you lie there soaked and aching, watching his new waterline disappear beneath the current.

encounters.title: A Road of Bones
encounters.flavor: White ribs of ancient driftwood cross a dry inlet like the bones of something huge, laid in a pattern too deliberate for any flood. A salvage guide says the road was here before her grandparents, though she will not say who built it. Sand rattles beneath the timbers whenever the wind moves.

choices.label: Cross on the old timbers
choices.intent: Pick your way across the old timbers yourself, testing each beam before you trust it.
choices.risk: The beams span the inlet, but the rot is hidden underneath each step.

success.text: Beneath the bleached beams you find braces that are still sound, and you step from one to the next. You reach the far bank before dusk, dusty and whole.

failure.text: A beam that looked sound splits under your weight and drops you into the rubble below. Bruised and limping, you take the long way around through the salt flats.

choices.label: Ask the guide to lead
choices.intent: Pay the guide from your pack to lead you across the sections she trusts.
choices.risk: A guide can save your crossing or strand you midway with less food.

success.text: She takes a share of your food as her fee, then admits which sections she has reinforced herself. She walks you across without a misstep and leaves you at the far bank with a nod.

failure.text: She takes her payment before setting foot on the old timbers. Halfway across, she slips between two ribs of driftwood and is gone. You spend the rest of the light finding solid footing for yourself. On the far bank your pack is lighter, and there is no one left to accuse.

encounters.title: The Reed Music
encounters.flavor: Music rises from a stretch of ground the map marks as empty. A lone reed player sits beside a trickle of fresh water and says the melody helps travelers hear when the buried river is moving. He plays on without looking up, and his feet never leave the dry ground.

choices.label: Listen between the notes
choices.intent: Sit still beside the reed player and listen for the river under the music.
choices.risk: The warning is quieter than the melody; one gust could hide the buried river's approach.

success.text: Under the melody you hear water moving beneath the sand. Beyond the musician's stone you find a shallow pool, clear and cold, and you fill every flask you carry.

failure.text: The wind rises and swallows the warning notes. You wander into a gust of grit that steals your breath and leaves you coughing, and it takes the rest of the day to recover.

choices.label: Offer an old traveling song
choices.intent: Answer his music with an old traveling song you learned on another road.
choices.risk: A song summons listeners you cannot see across the empty delta.

success.text: You answer with an old road song. For a moment the musician stops playing to hear someone else's voice; then he takes up your tune and threads a new river melody through it. When it ends, he points out a dry path that skirts the dangerous crossing. He asks you to remember the song.

failure.text: Your voice carries farther than you meant, and a patrol comes to see who is singing. You lie flat behind the rocks until they leave, and the heat wrings the strength out of you.

encounters.title: Hammer Under Stone
encounters.flavor: The abandoned quarry is not entirely abandoned. A lone mason taps the rock face with an iron hammer, listening to the stone, and refuses to work near a freshly cut seam. Someone has been quarrying here at night, he says, and they never set a single support under what they cut.

choices.label: Brace the loosened wall
choices.intent: Wedge a timber under the cracked shelf before it comes down on the path.
choices.risk: If the stone shifts before the brace holds, you are under it.

success.text: You drive the support home beneath the cracked shelf, and it holds. The mason clasps your hand, presses his flask and a packet of hard cheese on you, and walks you out the safe way.

failure.text: The stone slips before the brace takes the weight. It slams your back against the wall and buries the easy road under rubble, and you crawl free, hurting with every breath.

choices.label: Inspect the fresh cuts
choices.intent: Study the fresh chisel marks to learn who has been cutting here, and why.
choices.risk: Whoever made these cuts may still be close.

success.text: The chisel marks are neat and purposeful, and they point toward a side tunnel no map shows. Whoever reopened this quarry did it on purpose, and did it quietly.

failure.text: Loose shale skids out under your feet, and the clatter echoes down the seam. Voices answer from somewhere inside, and you scramble back the way you came, scraped and winded.

encounters.title: The Empty Pay Cart
encounters.flavor: An accountant counts pebbles into an empty ore cart where the wages should be. The workers are gone, but their names are still on a pay sheet pinned beneath his hoof. He offers you a share of whatever is left if you keep quiet about what you have seen.

choices.label: Refuse the crooked bargain
choices.intent: Turn down his money and tell him you will not help bury those names.
choices.risk: He may have guards nearby, paid better than his workers.

success.text: He studies you for a long moment, then sags. He leads you to the mouth of a tunnel and tells you it is where the missing workers last reported for their shift.

failure.text: He raises a hand, and guards step out of the dark. You get away through a rain of falling stone, but it batters you all the way to daylight.

choices.label: Read the pay sheet aloud
choices.intent: Pull the pay sheet out from under his hoof and read every name aloud.
choices.risk: If they take the sheet from you, the names go with it.

success.text: One by one, workers step out of the tunnels as they hear their names. They take back the cart and the supplies hidden under its pebbles, and they share bread and lamp oil with you before you go.

failure.text: Someone snatches the sheet before you reach the third name, and rough hands shove you into a narrow cut in the rock. You find your way out bruised, the names still unread.

encounters.title: The Glass Vein
encounters.flavor: A collector works alone at a vein of black glass that sings when it is struck. She knows the stuff can cut so cleanly that it does not bleed at first. She needs a steady hand to free one fragment for the road, and a strong back to carry the tray she has already filled.

choices.label: Cut a safe sample
choices.intent: Ease a small, blunt-edged shard out of the vein with her finest chisel.
choices.risk: The seam is brittle, and the glass cuts before you feel it.

success.text: The shard comes free whole, its edges dull enough to hold. In thanks, she marks a sheltered way out of the quarry and fills your pack with dried figs from her own store.

failure.text: The seam fractures under the chisel, and slivers spray across your hands. You pull back too late, and the cuts only start to bleed after you have walked away.

choices.label: Carry the collector's load
choices.intent: Shoulder her heavy tray of glass and carry it up the quarry wall.
choices.risk: One slip on the climb, and the whole tray shatters.

success.text: You climb slow and steady, and not one piece breaks. At the quarry rim she shares her supper with you and sends you on with the rest of it wrapped in cloth.

failure.text: A strap snaps halfway up. You catch the tray before it falls and every piece survives, but the weight wrenches your back and you finish the climb aching.

encounters.title: The Watchful Overhang
encounters.flavor: An ibex scout watches an overhang shed dust with every breeze. She warns that the canyon wall is moving faster than any weather can explain. Behind you, a line of travelers is already walking into its shadow, too tired to look up.

choices.label: Call the travelers back
choices.intent: Shout the travelers back out of the shadow before the wall comes down.
choices.risk: If they do not listen, you will be in there with them.

success.text: Your voice carries, and the caravan stops and turns. The scout leads everyone the long way around the crumbling shelf, and as you walk she shows you the old ledge paths only scouts use.

failure.text: Your warning comes too late for the last of them. You run back in and shield an old traveler as gravel rains down, and you both stagger out bruised and bleeding.

choices.label: Test the ledge alone
choices.intent: Go ahead alone, testing each foothold on the ledge before the others follow.
choices.risk: If the ledge gives way, there is a ravine beneath it.

success.text: You find the hollow stone beneath the path and mark every safe foothold for those behind you. The trail they walk now is not the one the old maps show.

failure.text: A loose slab tips you toward the ravine. The rope catches you, but it tears through your hands as you drop, and you haul yourself back up bleeding.

encounters.title: The Banner in the Wind
encounters.flavor: A torn banner snaps in the wind above a narrow bridge, tied where no courier would willingly stop. A captain searching for her missing rider studies its knotted corners. She insists the pattern is a call for help, not a warning to keep out, and she is running out of daylight to prove it.

choices.label: Decode the banner knots
choices.intent: Work out what the knots in the banner were tied to say.
choices.risk: The wind keeps twisting the cloth, and a misreading costs miles.

success.text: The knots describe a second bridge, older and hidden upstream. The captain listens, nods, and presses her last trail ration into your hands before she goes to look.

failure.text: The wind twists the cloth into nonsense, and you follow the meaning you think you see. It leads you on a long, exhausting detour that ends where it began.

choices.label: Search below the bridge
choices.intent: Climb down beneath the bridge in case the rider fell rather than fled.
choices.risk: The rock under the bridge is loose, and the drop is long.

success.text: Under the span you find the courier alive, wedged on a ledge with a broken strap. You help her climb up to the captain, who cannot speak for a moment.

failure.text: A foothold that looked solid crumbles, and you slide into a thicket of thorns above the riverbed. You climb out scratched and torn, with no sign of the rider.

encounters.title: The Toll Without a Keeper
encounters.flavor: A toll rope hangs across the canyon trail above a wooden box, and no one stands guard. The enforcer watches from the rocks overhead, waiting to see who will pay into an unattended box. Her spear has been deliberately blunted, as if she hopes never to use it.

choices.label: Challenge the false toll
choices.intent: Cut the toll rope and face the enforcer without raising a weapon against her.
choices.risk: She may not be the only one watching from the rocks.

success.text: You cut the rope and stand your ground without striking her. She comes down, looks at the frayed ends for a long time, and walks away from the box for good.

failure.text: Her partner comes at you from behind rocks you never thought to check. You get clear, but you are bruised and driven back down the trail.

choices.label: Offer a fair trade
choices.intent: Offer her food for honest word of the trail ahead instead of paying the box.
choices.risk: She may take your food and tell you nothing true.

success.text: She takes the provisions you offer and tells you exactly where the trail is failing. Then she lifts the rope and lets you and the travelers behind you pass.

failure.text: She takes the food, nods, and sends you down a fork that ends at a sheer drop. You climb back the long way, worn out and lighter by a meal.

encounters.title: One Place by the Fire
encounters.flavor: A camp keeps one empty place by its fire and one rule: no one asks why. The host waves you toward the seat while two exhausted travelers stare into their bowls. On the signboard behind them, someone has scraped a name away down to bare wood.

choices.label: Accept the offered place
choices.intent: Sit in the empty place, keep the rule, and listen to what goes unsaid.
choices.risk: Silence in a camp like this can turn ugly.

success.text: From what the travelers leave unsaid, you understand the missing one left by choice. The host fills a bowl for you without a word and, as the fire burns down, quietly names the safer road.

failure.text: An argument flares over the rule, and by midnight the camp has split in two. You stay up keeping watch between them and greet the morning exhausted.

choices.label: Ask about the missing name
choices.intent: Break the camp's rule and ask whose name was scraped from the board.
choices.risk: The rule exists for a reason; the camp may turn on you.

success.text: The host stares into the fire, then tells you the truth: a guide led travelers into the gorge and never came back. With a stick, the host draws you a way around it in the ash.

failure.text: The question splits the camp. To make peace, you hand your own food around the fire, and it is not enough; you leave before dawn under hostile stares, your pack lighter by a meal.

encounters.title: The Map in Ashes
encounters.flavor: An archivist feeds torn maps into the fire one corner at a time. She swears every version led some traveler into a trap. One fragment, already curling in the ashes, still shows a canyon notch you recognize, and the flames are almost on it.

choices.label: Rescue the marked fragment
choices.intent: Snatch the marked fragment out of the fire before it burns.
choices.risk: The embers are hot, and the paper is already curling.

success.text: You lift the fragment out whole and blow the sparks from its edge. Beside the notch, someone has crossed out one canyon path's name and written another: it was mislabeled on purpose.

failure.text: Embers sear your hand as you reach in, and the corner that mattered crumbles to ash between your fingers before you can read it.

choices.label: Persuade her to stop
choices.intent: Talk her away from the fire and ask what she is really afraid of.
choices.risk: She may burn the rest just to be rid of you.

success.text: Her hands go still. She admits she is afraid of sending anyone else to die, then gives you an untouched chart with a safe camp marked in ink, and a twist of tea and salt from her own pack.

failure.text: She shakes her head and tips the whole stack into the fire. You watch every route burn and walk on with no better guidance than you had before.

encounters.title: The Night Watch Debt
encounters.flavor: A retired sentry offers to watch the camp tonight, on one condition: whoever accepts will owe him a night's sleep in return. His lantern has no lens, yet he walks the perimeter with practiced care. At every circuit he stops to count footsteps that belong to no one in camp.

choices.label: Take the first watch
choices.intent: Pay the debt up front by taking the first watch so the old sentry can rest.
choices.risk: You are already tired, and the dark here is crowded.

success.text: Near midnight you catch a thief creeping toward the supply packs and send him running. The sentry wakes, hears what happened, calls the debt paid, and presses a share of the saved food on you.

failure.text: Exhaustion blurs the dark into shapes. You fight to stay on your feet, and while you do, thieves slip in and carry off the camp's food, your own with it.

choices.label: Follow the counted footsteps
choices.intent: Follow the footsteps the sentry keeps counting to find who is circling the camp.
choices.risk: The canyon throws echoes, and not every sound is a step.

success.text: The tracks lead to a lost pilgrim, frightened and harmless, who has been circling the fires too afraid to call out. You bring her in before the camp wakes to panic.

failure.text: You follow what you take for footsteps until you realize they are only echoes. By then you are deep in a cold gully, and you spend the night there shivering until morning.

encounters.title: Feathers in the Draft
encounters.flavor: At the cave mouth, a crow storm-reader pins paper charms into the wind, and not one tears loose. A cold draft keeps returning from the wrong direction, carrying black feathers that never settle. She says the cavern remembers spoken bargains better than faces, and she will not let you pass until you have answered her.

choices.label: Answer her question plainly
choices.intent: Tell her your name and your business straight, the way the cavern will hear it.
choices.risk: A careless word here could echo where you don't want it.

success.text: You give your name and nothing more. The storm-reader repeats it once into the wind, nods, and draws a chalk sign on your palm that marks the safe entrance.

failure.text: Your answer comes back from three passages at once, and you follow the wrong one. The cold pocket at its end drains the warmth from your hands before you find your way out, shivering and spent.

choices.label: Study the returning draft
choices.intent: Watch where the feathers go and find what keeps pushing the air back out.
choices.risk: The wind is strong, and the cave floor drops without warning.

success.text: You follow a feather to a narrow vent where the wind doubles back on itself. That explains the echo, and you scratch a mark beside the passage below that you know you can trust.

failure.text: The draft snuffs your lantern halfway down. You hurry on in the dark, and sharp stone tears at your knees and hands before you crawl back to the grey light of the mouth.

encounters.title: The Third Shadow
encounters.flavor: A guide offers to lead you underground, but three shadows stretch behind her from only two lanterns. She insists the third belongs to a traveler who turned back this morning. At the entrance, a line of marker stones has been moved since sunrise, and she will not look at it.

choices.label: Count the lantern positions
choices.intent: Work out where a hidden third light must be to cast that shadow.
choices.risk: Guess wrong, and whoever holds that light strikes first.

success.text: You trace the angle back to a shuttered lamp in a crevice, where two trappers crouch waiting. Named aloud, they slip away without a fight, and the guide's face goes grey with shame.

failure.text: You turn toward the wrong shadow. A trapper's cord whips out of the dark and opens a cut across your shoulder, and you are bleeding by the time you scramble back into daylight.

choices.label: Demand a safer passage
choices.intent: Tell the guide you know it's a trap, and ask for the honest way down.
choices.risk: Her friends may not like being found out.

success.text: The guide drops the act. Her brother owes the trappers, she says, and this was his payment. In exchange for your mercy, she shows you a real lower corridor, dry and clear.

failure.text: Her accomplices step out and block the gate. You fight your way free, bruised from the scuffle, but your food sack stays behind in their hands.

encounters.title: Shelter for the Storm
encounters.flavor: Rain lashes the ridge as a healer drags a medicine chest toward the cave. Travelers stranded by the sudden storm huddle under the overhang behind her, and her lamp gutters with every gust. Below them, water is already rising over the ledge they must cross to reach real shelter.

choices.label: Carry the medicine chest
choices.intent: Take the heavy chest so the healer's hands are free for the injured.
choices.risk: The stone is slick, and the chest is heavier than it looks.

success.text: You get the chest into the dry without cracking a single vial. The healer presses a roll of bandage and a heel of bread into your hands, and sketches the dry passage on the back of a label.

failure.text: The chest slips on wet stone and comes down hard on your knee. You lift it again and finish the climb, but every step after reminds you of it.

choices.label: Guide the stranded travelers
choices.intent: Lead the frightened travelers across the ledge before the water takes it.
choices.risk: Fear spreads fast in a storm, and the ledge is narrow.

success.text: You keep your voice low and steady, and they cross one at a time behind you. Once inside, an old drover splits his last dried apples with you and won't hear a refusal.

failure.text: Thunder breaks over the ridge and the group scatters. You spend a cold hour calling them back down the slope, and somewhere in the dark a meal spills from your pack into the runoff.

encounters.title: The Candle Court
encounters.flavor: Deep in the hollow, an adjudicator holds court by candlelight, a hundred small flames ringing a slab of stone. Two miners each claim the same pouch of pale salt, and the only witness has not come. No one may leave until the matter is settled, and the adjudicator asks you to weigh the evidence.

choices.label: Hear both testimonies
choices.intent: Listen to each miner in full and look for what their stories leave out.
choices.risk: A rehearsed lie can sound more honest than the truth.

success.text: You notice a fresh tear in the pouch that matches a tear in one miner's sleeve. The adjudicator divides the salt by what you found, and the guilty miner pays without arguing.

failure.text: You believe the smoother story. The wronged miner, a broad woman with salt-cracked hands, catches you outside the candlelight and lands one hard blow before the clerks pull her away.

choices.label: Offer a shared judgment
choices.intent: Propose they split the salt before witnesses, so neither has to be called a thief.
choices.risk: Neither miner may be willing to give an inch.

success.text: Both miners grumble, then agree to a witnessed split. The adjudicator lets you pass without owing the court anything, and snuffs the candle nearest the door in your honor.

failure.text: Neither miner will budge, and the hearing drags through the night. By the time the candles gutter, you have shared most of your food with the hungry court just to keep tempers cool.

encounters.title: Salt on the Threshold
encounters.flavor: A mason has laid a thick line of salt across a narrow doorway, though the stone beyond looks ordinary. She swears the salt keeps the cavern air from turning poisonous when the pressure shifts, and her measurements are scratched across a slab of slate. The vent above the door is cracked, and the shift is close.

choices.label: Reinforce the vent above
choices.intent: Shore up the cracked vent over the door without breaking the salt seal below.
choices.risk: One slip of the chisel could break the seal.

success.text: You pack the crack and ease the vent open without moving a grain of salt. The mason grins, shares a strip of smoked fish from her pack, and tells you which turn past the doorway she trusts.

failure.text: The seal breaks under your chisel. Stinging dust pours from the vent and fills the room, and you stagger out with streaming eyes and a raw, burning chest.

choices.label: Test the air carefully
choices.intent: Hold a flame at the salt line and breathe slowly, checking whether her warning holds.
choices.risk: If the air turns while you're testing it, you're inside.

success.text: The flame bends and a faint mineral smell rises off the stone. Her warning is true. You find a clean way around along the upper shelf, and the salt line stays whole.

failure.text: You take too long. Dust floods the chalked passage and you back out coughing, your throat raw and your chest aching for the next mile.

encounters.title: The Forgotten Pledge
encounters.flavor: A guardian stands before a sealed chamber, repeating an oath in a voice he no longer recognizes as his own. The iron charm on his wrist glows only when he tries to step away. A ritual put it there, and he watches you as if you might remember the pledge he has forgotten.

choices.label: Speak the oath back to him
choices.intent: Repeat his oath slowly, in your own voice, so he can hear where it changed.
choices.risk: The binding may answer before he does.

success.text: You speak the words back to him and he follows them like a rope out of deep water. He remembers who bound the charm, and unseals the safe way through.

failure.text: The binding surges through the chamber. The guardian's arm swings without his consent and strikes you hard, and he is weeping apologies as you limp away.

choices.label: Examine the iron charm
choices.intent: Look closely at the charm for the catch that holds it shut.
choices.risk: Charms like this are often built to punish curious hands.

success.text: You find a fastening hidden under the scrollwork and work it loose. The charm drops to the stone. The guardian offers you everything he has, and you take nothing; he needs it more.

failure.text: The clasp you press is false. It snaps shut on your fingers and a shock runs up your arm, throwing you clear of the guardian with your hand numb and burning.

encounters.title: Three Doors Without Hinges
encounters.flavor: Three stone doorways stand where four tunnels ought to meet: open arches with no hinges and nothing to close. An architect traces the missing route with a measuring chain, explaining that tremors shift these crossings while their destinations stay put. Her diagram, she admits, is accurate only for this hour.

choices.label: Compare the chain marks
choices.intent: Match the scratches her chain left on each arch to find the one that hasn't moved.
choices.risk: The slabs move without warning, and corridors can close.

success.text: One arch carries an old fracture that lines up with every mark. You copy the new arrangement of the tunnels into your notes, and the way ahead redraws itself around the doorway that holds true.

failure.text: The chain snags beneath a grinding slab. You tear it free and squeeze out of the narrowing corridor, bruised along your arms and ribs.

choices.label: Ask someone to witness your path
choices.intent: Ask the architect to send someone with you, so your choice of door is on record.
choices.risk: She may spare no one, and you could end up choosing alone.

success.text: The architect sends a quiet novice to walk with you. Neither of you can later deny which door you took, and the novice's chalk marks keep you from doubling back.

failure.text: Her apprentice refuses to go. You choose alone, second-guess every turn, and give a night's sleep to the maze before you trust your footing, coming out hollow with exhaustion.

encounters.title: Voices Across the Rock
encounters.flavor: A courier calls out from behind a sheet of stone, but his voice arrives through the wrong tunnel. He says he carries a letter for a village beyond the cave, and a second, flatter voice repeats his words a moment later. The rock between you shivers with underground thunder.

choices.label: Trace the true echo
choices.intent: Follow the first voice, not its copy, to find where the courier really is.
choices.risk: The false echo leads somewhere too.

success.text: You press your ear to the stone until you find the thin place where his voice sounds warm. You chip a gap, pull him through, and lead him up into open air, his letter still dry.

failure.text: The false echo draws you into a low passage just as grit pours from the ceiling. You scrape your arm raw dragging yourself clear.

choices.label: Signal a safe meeting point
choices.intent: Tap a steady pattern on the stone and keep it up until he finds you.
choices.risk: Thunder may swallow the signal, and the search could run long.

success.text: You tap and wait, tap and wait, until the courier stumbles out of a side corridor. He laughs with relief and splits his spare meal with you before going on.

failure.text: Thunder drowns the taps. You keep the search alive for hours, eating through your food to stay sharp, and by the time the courier finds you, your pack is much lighter.

encounters.title: The Red Vial
encounters.flavor: An exhausted pilgrim crouches over a red vial and begs strangers not to come close. He says the liquid holds back a hunger a sorcerer laid on him, and that he has not slept in days. His hands shake so badly that the flask seems more dangerous than he is.

choices.label: Help secure the vial
choices.intent: Steady his hands and wrap the flask somewhere it can't break.
choices.risk: If it shatters, neither of you knows what happens.

success.text: You wrap the flask in a leather cradle and buckle it against his chest. His breathing slows. Before you part, he tells you about a tunnel the sorcerer's people never watch.

failure.text: The vial lurches and nearly shatters. In his panic the pilgrim shoves you hard into the rock wall, then cries out an apology as you pick yourself up, bruised and winded.

choices.label: Ask about the binding spell
choices.intent: Ask gently how the spell was cast, looking for a weakness in it.
choices.risk: He may hear the question as an accusation.

success.text: Among the scratches he draws for you, you recognize a counter-sign. You teach it to him slowly, and for the first time his hands go still around the vial.

failure.text: He hears accusation in your question and lunges. The struggle is short and desperate, and you both end up gasping on the cave floor, the vial unbroken and your ribs aching.

encounters.title: The Cooling Stones
encounters.flavor: The black road holds its warmth long after sunset. A road mender taps a line of stones that glow faintly under her hammer, and warns you that an old fissure opens here as the ground cools. Down the road, the lanterns of the next caravan are already in sight.

choices.label: Mark the unsafe seam
choices.intent: Find where the fissure will open and wave the caravan away from it.
choices.risk: The seam may open while you're standing on it.

success.text: You trace the seam to its end and find solid ground around it. Your lantern swings the caravan onto the detour just before the road splits, and the way ahead now bends around a fresh black gap.

failure.text: The road parts beneath your feet. You throw yourself back, but the edge of the stone cuts deep into your leg before you reach solid ground.

choices.label: Help lay a new crossing
choices.intent: Haul slabs with the mender to bridge the gap before the caravan arrives.
choices.risk: The slabs are heavy, and the ground beneath them is moving.

success.text: Together you lever the last slab into place as the first wagon rolls up. The drivers cross safely, and the mender fills your waterskin from the caravan's barrel in thanks.

failure.text: The slabs shift under your weight and slide into the fissure. You claw your way back up the hot rock, scraped and burning, while your supplies tumble into the dark below.

encounters.title: A Mirror in the Ash
encounters.flavor: On a road buried in ash, a scavenger turns a mirror toward the empty horizon and watches dust settle on its face. She claims it shows travelers what they have already lost, though her own reflection stays ordinary. Beside the mirror lies a scatter of discarded letters, some never opened.

choices.label: Read the discarded letters
choices.intent: Sort through the letters she threw away, looking for something she missed.
choices.risk: The wind up here does not wait for slow readers.

success.text: One letter mentions a dry well and a cairn by the road, written by someone who meant to come back. It explains nothing about the mirror, but you fold it carefully and keep it.

failure.text: A gust tears the letters from your hands and scatters them down the slope. You chase them across the open ridge until the cold and the ash leave you worn through.

choices.label: Trade a true memory
choices.intent: Give the scavenger an honest memory of something you lost, as she asks.
choices.risk: Some memories cost more to say aloud than you expect.

success.text: You tell her about a loss you rarely speak of, and she listens without interrupting. When you finish, she points out a sheltered way past the ruins and asks for nothing more.

failure.text: The memory comes out harder than you meant, and grief follows it. You stumble on past the mirror, unable to steady yourself, and walk the next miles bone-tired.

encounters.title: Ashes at the Border
encounters.flavor: At the border, a ranger stops you while ash drifts across the road like snow. She guards a damaged watchtower and will let no one through until its signal horn is mended. Her comrades left hours ago for water, and she keeps glancing at the empty trail they took.

choices.label: Repair the signal horn
choices.intent: Clear the horn's jammed valve so the ranger can sound the all-clear.
choices.risk: The horn is old, and breaking it would cost you.

success.text: You scrape packed ash from the valve and the horn finds its voice. The ranger sounds the warning, one long low note across the border, and waves you through the barrier.

failure.text: The horn splits in your hands. The stranded ranger, furious, demands payment for it, and you hand over most of your food because you have nothing else to give.

choices.label: Offer to scout the tower
choices.intent: Climb the damaged tower and look for what the ranger can't see from the road.
choices.risk: The stairs are cracked, and ash hides the worst of it.

success.text: From the top you spot a dust front rolling toward the road. You shout down in time, and you and the ranger shelter behind the tower wall until it passes.

failure.text: The stairs crumble under you halfway up. You make it down just ahead of the falling stones, bruised all over and coughing ash.

encounters.title: The Last Watchfire
encounters.flavor: The camp's last watchfire burns low beside a stack of good dry wood. Its commander says the guards refuse to light a second flame while refugees are still lost outside the barricade. Her sabre rests untouched beside the gate, and no one has offered to go out into the dark.

choices.label: Volunteer for the search
choices.intent: Go out past the barricade yourself and bring the missing refugees in.
choices.risk: The dark beyond the camp hides a ravine, and worse.

success.text: You follow faint calls into the dark and come back with every one of them. A grandmother among the refugees pushes a cloth of dried figs into your hand and holds on a moment too long.

failure.text: You reach the ravine too late; the tracks end at its edge. You climb back along the narrow path, scraped and shaking, and the commander does not ask what you found.

choices.label: Organize the watch rota
choices.intent: Draw up a fair rotation so the guards can search and still hold the gate.
choices.risk: Tired guards don't take orders kindly from a stranger.

success.text: The camp accepts a fair split of duty, and a fresh patrol goes out at once. The quartermaster, grateful for a night's sleep, sends you off with bread from the stores.

failure.text: Old grudges split the patrol, and someone blames the stranger. You are sent out of the camp before a watch can be set, and the ration you set down by the fire stays behind.

encounters.title: The Closed Infirmary
encounters.flavor: A field physician keeps wounded travelers waiting outside an infirmary whose door has been nailed shut. She insists the room is contaminated, but the only bandages in camp are inside. Guards crowd around a half-unloaded supply wagon, accusing her of inventing the danger, and one already has a crowbar in hand.

choices.label: Inspect the sealed room
choices.intent: Pry a board loose and see for yourself what is behind the door.
choices.risk: If she is right, the air in there could poison you.

success.text: Inside you find spoiled herbs rotting in a sack, not plague. You haul out the clean bandages, and the physician, embarrassed and grateful, packs some for your own road.

failure.text: You force the door too fast and breathe in a lungful of bitter fumes. You stagger back weak and retching, and the physician has to treat you first.

choices.label: Calm the waiting guards
choices.intent: Talk the guards down before they break the door and spread whatever is inside.
choices.risk: A frightened crowd turns quickly.

success.text: You remind the guards there are clean supplies on the wagon behind them. They lower the crowbar and carry bandages to the wounded instead of breaking down the door.

failure.text: Someone shouts plague and the crowd surges. The wagon goes over, and in the crush you take an elbow to the jaw and a knee to the ribs.

encounters.title: The Prisoner of Dusk
encounters.flavor: Guards hold a scout whose eyes flash red whenever sunlight touches the copper wire on his wrists. A medic says it began after he handled an occult relic out in the waste. The sun is sinking toward the ridge, and the commander keeps her hand on her sword, waiting to see what dusk will do to him.

choices.label: Question the scout quietly
choices.intent: Sit with the scout and ask what he touched, before the guards lose their nerve.
choices.risk: If his voice turns, the guards will strike first.

success.text: In a low voice he tells you where the relic lies buried. You persuade the commander to loosen the wire under guard, and his eyes stay his own as dusk falls.

failure.text: His voice slips into something that is not his, and the guards panic. You step between them and him, and take a spear shaft across the shoulders for it.

choices.label: Secure the copper restraint
choices.intent: Mend the damaged clasp on his wire so it holds without cutting him.
choices.risk: The copper runs hot when the light touches it.

success.text: You rebuild the clasp so it holds firm without biting into his skin. It buys enough time for a healer to arrive, and the scout thanks you with his eyes shut tight.

failure.text: The clasp heats in your grip and burns your palm. You cry out, the scout thrashes, and the guards drive you away from the prisoner with your hand blistered.

encounters.title: The Key Without a Door
encounters.flavor: An archivist waits beside an unmarked gate, holding out a key carved from stone. She says it belongs to a door no one has ever found twice, and the gate behind her has no lock at all. Faded carvings on the gatepost show travelers arriving from every direction, each by a different road.

choices.label: Read the worn carving
choices.intent: Study the carvings for a mark that repeats, whatever road each traveler came by.
choices.risk: Old stone crumbles, and the archivist may lose patience.

success.text: Under the grime you find one mark repeated in every figure. Laid against the road you actually walked, it lines the gate up with your own steps, and the archivist nods slowly.

failure.text: The pattern crumbles under your rubbing. The archivist sends you down a side passage to try another way, and its loose scree throws you down hard twice before you climb back out.

choices.label: Ask who forged the key
choices.intent: Ask her plainly who made the key and what they wanted with it.
choices.risk: She may hear suspicion where you mean only curiosity.

success.text: She admits she does not know who made it; it was handed to her the way she now offers it to you. Then she shows you how to approach the gate without waking its old warding.

failure.text: She hears an accusation in your question and ends the audience. The supplies you set down as a courtesy gift stay with her, and you walk away with a lighter pack.

encounters.title: A Promise Kept
encounters.flavor: A messenger rests just short of the final gate, one hand flat on a sealed letter that has crossed several kingdoms. Its recipient may have vanished long ago, but she promised to deliver it. She has begun to wonder aloud whether a duty can outlive its purpose, and she cannot carry it much farther alone.

choices.label: Carry the sealed letter
choices.intent: Take the letter from her and promise to finish its journey, seal unbroken.
choices.risk: Another person's promise is heavy to carry on a hard road.

success.text: You take the letter and do not open it. The messenger, lighter for it, gives you the last of her trail bread and the final safe directions she has carried this far.

failure.text: The letter weighs on your thoughts more than your pack does. In the narrow pass you misstep and wrench your ankle, and the climb takes more out of you than it should.

choices.label: Help search for its owner
choices.intent: Search the road for any trace of the letter's recipient before giving up.
choices.risk: The trail is old, and searching will cost you time.

success.text: Together you find a sign scratched into a waystone, left by the recipient for whoever came after. It confirms the road you are already on, and the messenger walks the rest of it with you, certain now.

failure.text: The search turns up only old tracks, half buried in ash. The delay eats into your stores, and at the roadside you share your last meal with the messenger.

encounters.title: The Price of Silence
encounters.flavor: A negotiator offers you passage on one condition: you must never speak of what you see beyond the gate. No contract names the powers who set that price of silence. She waits without anger, hands folded, as the black stones cool at her feet.

choices.label: Refuse the secret bargain
choices.intent: Turn down her offer and look for a way past the gate that binds you to nothing.
choices.risk: Without her help, the only other ways are rough ones.

success.text: You decline, and she lets you. Following the old wall, you find a gap in the stones around her seal, unbound and unwatched, and you walk through it owing no one.

failure.text: She closes the direct gate without a word. The only way left is over a razor-edged ridge of obsidian, and you reach the far side with cut hands and torn knees.

choices.label: Question the cost openly
choices.intent: Ask her, in front of the others waiting, what silence actually costs.
choices.risk: She may simply keep you talking until night falls.

success.text: After a long pause, she admits the price is obedience, not coin. You refuse the bargain and walk away with the truth of it intact, which is more than most travelers get.

failure.text: She answers in riddles until dusk. By then you have eaten through more of your food than you meant to, and night comes down cold and open around you.
